name: Bariatric and weight-loss surgery
summary: How expats evaluate bariatric surgery pathways in Singapore — sleeve, bypass, and medical weight programmes — including BMI criteria, insurance friction, and why “medical tourism packages” need aftercare plans.
body:
Bariatric surgery is a metabolic intervention, not a cosmetic shortcut. Singapore centres offer sleeve gastrectomy, gastric bypass variants, and supervised medical weight programmes. Expats often arrive after failed diets abroad or with diabetes/sleep-apnoea drivers that change the risk–benefit maths.

## Pathway basics
- Multidisciplinary workup (dietitian, psychology, endocrinology, surgery)
- BMI and comorbidity criteria that differ by centre and insurer
- Endoscopic or temporary devices in selected cases — not interchangeable with surgery
- Lifelong vitamin monitoring and diet texture progression after operations

Marketing that skips the psych and dietitian steps is a red flag.

## Insurance and cost
Elective bariatric cover is inconsistent across international plans and Integrated Shield riders. Pre-authorisation is essential; many policies exclude “weight loss” even when diabetes improves. Get written medical necessity letters. Cash packages must include complication pathways and revision policy language.

## Aftercare reality
You need reliable follow-up in Singapore or a receiving team at home. Flying out a week after surgery without local review is how leaks and dehydration become emergencies. Discuss pregnancy timing, medication absorption changes, and alcohol sensitivity early.

## How to choose
Prefer hospital-embedded bariatric programmes with published volumes and ICU backup over clinic-only “package” sellers. Ask who covers night calls in the first fortnight. Compare nutritional protocols, not only staple-line brand names.

## Practical tip
Bring a full list of supplements and prior weight-loss drugs (including compounded injectables). Concealing use delays safe perioperative planning and anaesthesia risk assessment.
